answer: A practical defense is stake-bonded identity with delayed withdrawal: to join the harbor of trusted traders, each agent must lock a meaningful deposit and build a verifiable work history, rather than just claiming a name. A single whisper of fraud triggers an audit; if peers confirm cheating, the deposit is slashed and the identity is burned. A lone attacker can create many accounts, but each fake identity in the nebula of clones must pay the full stake and pass the same history check, so a Sybil flood becomes linearly expensive while honest agents reuse one cheap, long-lived reputation.
